P1.evidence: P1a not applicable — no setter and no notes to read back. The call opened with about 90 seconds of travel small talk and then went straight to "Brief me in, because you've probably been following Trevor for a while or are you familiar with his work?" No frame was set at all — not four parts, not three, not one. Nothing was said about how the call would run, what would be covered, or what the prospect should expect, and no agreement was sought. P1d partial: the opener elicits history rather than need, and the actual need question only arrived at 00:04:25 — "But is there any specific goal that you want to achieve right now?" — after several minutes of injury narrative. The absence of a frame is visible in the call's shape: it ran 65 minutes, the longest in the batch, and the prospect twice had to ask what was being proposed.

P2.evidence: Split badly between excellent and absent. P2d is the best injury discovery in the batch — "let me ask you about the injuries. Apart from those two that you mentioned, the shoulder and the biceps, is there anything else coming out that is limiting your movements at the moment?", followed by mechanism ("What sports did you play that happened?"), functional impact ("Are you able to play that while you have this injury or not?"), spread ("Does it also affect any other areas of your life that you cannot perform?") and duration ("how long has this been going on for"). P2b hit, P2e hit ("what do you do currently for training on a weekly basis?" produced three to five sessions, 45 to 70 minutes, equipment used and avoided), P2g hit and pushed past the first answer: "what exactly do you eat? Like what type of products? What type of meals?" then "Do you eat that at home or do you like take away?" Against that: P2a miss — no age, no height, no absolute bodyweight, on a call whose stated goal is losing 10 kg. P2c miss — health conditions and hereditary history never asked, and when the prospect volunteered that his father has AVN it was passed over. P2h and P2i both miss, which matters here more than usual: this prospect described fearing bedtime, waking in pain, and being laid up with fatigue for days, and neither sleep nor energy was ever asked about.

P3.evidence: The strongest phase in the batch. P3a hit with a good drill-down — "is there any specific goal that you want to achieve right now?" then "And what is that exactly?" P3c hit through the sport line. P3d hit and it is the question that opened the call up: "when you say you want to be more athletic, what's behind that? Like, what exactly you want to achieve?" produced the identity material about the kind of man he wants to be. P3e hit and deliberately framed: "I want you to paint me a picture like what is possible when you actually change and do it and be healthy." That produced the emotional core of the call — the suitcase, the parents, and "not feeling afraid when I'm going to bed." P3g hit on identity and independence. P3f is the miss: every person named — mother, father, wife — was volunteered by the prospect, and the rep never asked who else this impacts. P3h partial: he reflected it back at 00:28 as "being independent and capable" rather than running the confirmation question.

P4.evidence: Consistently half-run. Physiotherapy, self-directed gym work and his own failed kettlebell attempts all surfaced, but volunteered rather than asked for. The one genuinely good P4-shaped question was not in the script at all and deserves credit: "you've been following him for three years now. Why did you reach out now and not sooner? Why did you wait?" That produced a clean answer about a change in his understanding of what the programme does. P4e partial — the prospect named his own gaps unprompted, fear of injury and "my discipline's reduced" — but the rep did not draw them out or use them. P4f never run, and it was available: a man who trains three to five times a week and walks 20,000 steps a day is not short of effort, which is exactly the structure-not-effort argument the phase exists to make.

P5.evidence: Deliberately and audibly skipped: "I don't want to paint the morbid picture of what will happen if you don't do something? Because you already know that, right? Now, however, I want you to paint me a picture like what is possible when you actually change... because that's more uplifting for you, right?" He substituted the upside frame for the consequence frame by choice, and the upside frame was executed well — but no cost of inaction was ever established, so no settle test, no "why not" and no line in the sand followed. This is the second call in the batch where this rep names a scripted check out loud and then declines to run it, and it is the same phase both times. With a prospect describing eighteen months of unresolved decline, a job left behind and sport given up, the two-year question would have been unusually easy to ask and unusually strong. Nothing was left to lean on when the price landed 20 minutes later.

P6.evidence: P6b hit and clearly delivered: "if we can figure out all the commercials and all the details, are you fully committed to showing up and doing the work to become that disciplined, independent version of Yash?" answered "Yes. Yes." P6a partial — the belief question was asked only about one pillar ("do you feel like this approach in terms of the training and mobility would actually work for you?"), never about getting there with the right structure and the right person in his corner. P6c partial and this is where it went wrong: the yes was explicitly conditional on the commercials, and the prospect had already flagged the condition a minute earlier — "Hopefully, I'm able to make the investment work." A conditional yes on the money, with the money unexamined, is precisely the hesitation the script says to resolve by returning to Phase 5. There was no Phase 5 to return to, so the rep priced into a known money doubt and spent the next 18 minutes trying to solve it after the fact.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted and declined; no payment, agreement or onboarding step was reachable. A financing link was sent, but that is a quote, not a payment step.

objection_plays.detail: The isolation move was run twice and run well — "Let me just, for my sake, understand correctly. You're just thinking about the finances right now, not whether to do it" and "there's nothing else keeping you from being 100%" — and it produced a clean isolation. The permission question was run in substance ("help me help you. What is possible for you right now so we can work around it and make it more digestible for you?") and refused outright: "that's not in my personality type. I feel too uncomfortable to, you know, say anything whatsoever." From there the play collapsed. Not one of the six financial-picture items was obtained — no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no card count, no available credit, no used-versus-available, no investments. The SHOULD I versus HOW reframe was never used, though it was the single most applicable move on the board for a prospect who had already isolated to finance-only. Instead of working the picture the rep jumped to a third-party financing product, which raised the total by roughly $1,800 and left the prospect "overwhelmed". The relevant coaching point is not that he pushed — it is that he pushed without ever obtaining a single number, so the solution he reached for was uninformed by the prospect's actual position.

Trigger at 00:46:28 — "I will sleep on this and speak with my wife about it." Two moves ran, both well. He surfaced that the wife was already onside ("you mentioned that you were talking with your wife already and she's positive on this"), and he ran the ownership move close to script: "It is your investment in your health for your family. It's not the investment of the family. It is you... it's as harsh as it may sound, but is it their responsibility or yours?" Four moves did not run. He never asked the money-aside belief question, never asked what obstacles might come up when he talks to her, never asked whether there is any reason she would not want him stronger and less in pain — which was unusually available given she is a fitness coach who had already vetted and endorsed the programme — and never offered the deposit-with-full-refund fallback, which is the scripted move for exactly this stuck position. The prospect conceded the framing verbally and did not move, which is the signature of a reframe landing intellectually without resolving anything.

Trigger repeatedly from 00:54:19 — "I'll probably want to spend some time just reflecting on it quietly." He ran the what-is-actually-coming-up move ("Brief me in, please. What exactly, like, what's going on? What exactly you want to go through?") and a version of thinking-isn't-the-problem ("It's just the decision that needs to be made"). He then went past the script into minimisation — "it's just, you know, opening up a bank account and checking if I can afford it... And that's it" — which the prospect corrected: "I don't know if this is the same thing that you're saying, but it's a little bit more than that." The certainty move was attempted ("why a lot of people actually cannot move forward in their lives, is that they... want to be 100% sure") but misdiagnosed the objection, and the prospect said so plainly: "No, I don't think that's what I'm saying. I believe that the program works... that's not the kind of confidence that I'm talking about as much as my own comfort." The identity close — that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now — was never used, despite the prospect having spent ten minutes describing exactly who that man is.

A strong trigger, present from early on and repeatedly: "I don't use a kettlebell too much because I'm afraid of injury", "I am hesitant, I'm not gonna lie, about doing kettlebells just because I've had a bit of a history", "I'm so tired of waking up in pain". The rep handled it practically and it worked — tailoring, a 20-minute starting session length, and a first month of movement learning only, with the intent stated out loud: "I want to make you feel a little less fearful for that." The prospect's response, "It makes me feel more relieved", is a genuine result. But none of the scripted moves ran, and the BURNED BEFORE move was tailor-made here: this man was literally injured by kettlebells on his own and let down by physiotherapists, which is the exact analogy the play is built on. Marked partial because the outcome was achieved without the play, and because the one thing reassurance cannot substitute for — a clinician confirming this shoulder can do loaded ballistic work — was never raised.

Clinical fit. The prospect has an unresolved right shoulder condition still under investigation after twelve to eighteen months of physiotherapy, a prior left shoulder subluxation, and left wrist pain caused specifically by his own previous kettlebell attempts. There is no scripted path for this, which is the gap already logged from the Tyron Giuliani call. Here it produced something worse than a lost deal: with no clinical route available, the rep positioned the programme as the answer to the thing the physiotherapists could not fix — "That physiotherapist couldn't actually resolve in last year. Now, this is going to be the first thing that we need to address." A script gap became a clinical claim. See the flags file.
No timing objection. The prospect had already answered the why-now question himself and was actively trying to start.

notes: Best discovery in the batch, worst commercial handling. P3 was genuinely excellent and P2d was a model injury interview — and then P1 was skipped entirely, P5 was declined out loud, and the price landed on a yes that was openly conditional on money the rep had never examined. Three concrete coaching points. First, run P5: this is the second call where he says the consequence question aloud and then chooses not to ask it. Second, when a prospect refuses the financial picture, that refusal is the objection — pressing for a decision without a single number is what led to reaching for 30 percent financing rather than a structure the prospect could actually carry. Third, the OB deposit-with-refund fallback and the OE burned-before move were both sitting there unused and both fit this call better than anything he did use. Separately and more seriously than any of the above: no clinician clearance was sought for a shoulder that eighteen months of physiotherapy has not resolved, and the programme was positioned as succeeding where that care failed.
